subject: OrionAI dedicated capacity - scaling constraints & traffic inventory

From: Samantha Park <samantha.p@orionai.com>

Cc: Ops Team <ops@orionai.com>
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: OrionAI dedicated capacity - traffic inventory and constraints

Hi Dylan / Marissa,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're moving toward a Reserved/Dedicated engagement and need to provide a traffic inventory so your pre-sales team can size a fleet and quote commits. I've attached a small telemetry sample from this week (orionai_telemetry_sample.csv). High-level asks below — please confirm if you need different granularity.

- Current production baseline: 120 rps sustained (API-level requests/sec across both inference and embedding endpoints)
- Peak observed: 1,900 rps for 90s during product launch (UTC: 2026-08-04T20:11Z)
- Prompt/response token distribution (approx): prompt median 120 tokens, 95th 780 tokens; response median 140 tokens, 95th 980 tokens
- Session model usage: ~60% single-turn stateless requests, ~40% multi-turn with KV cache; average session length 2.4 turns, p95 session duration 18 minutes
- Model variants: mixture of open-weights LLM v2 (primary) + reranker/embedding models for subset of endpoints
- Target p95 tail latency: 450ms for interactive endpoints (we can tolerate 1.5s for long-form generation)
- Tolerance for soft degradation: prefer graceful fallback to a quantized variant over outright 429
- Expected ramp: 2x sustained within 9 months; commit horizon 12 months

Questions for you (we can provide raw telemetry if helpful):
1) Will you need per-route concurrency limits modeled or is a single pool assumption OK?
2) How do you treat KV cache residency for sizing (counted as resident memory per session)?
3) Any recommendations for GPU SKUs given the mix above and desire to reduce cost while keeping tail latency?

Thanks — attaching the CSV and a short summary PDF. Happy to hop on a quick 30-min cadence next week.

Best,
Samantha Park
Head of Infrastructure, OrionAI
Samantha.P@orionai.com

Attachments: orionai_telemetry_sample.csv (csv, 320KB), orionai_request_summary.pdf (pdf, 80KB)

Subject: Re: OrionAI dedicated capacity - traffic inventory and constraints

Samantha — thanks for the detail and the telemetry sample, this is very helpful.

Quick read on next steps from my side:
- I attached a one-page dedicated sizing template (dedicated_sizing_template.xlsx) for canonical fields we load into our sizing engine. If you can fill the highlighted rows (avg/peak RPS per route, prompt/response percentile tokens, session affinity flags) that speeds things up.
- High-level answers inline to your questions:
  1) We prefer per-route concurrency when there are mixed SLOs (interactive vs long-form). If you want a simple starting point we can run a single-pool estimate then show per-route delta.
  2) KV cache: we model resident KV as per-session memory consumption; for pooled workloads we size for the expected active session set (p99 concurrent sessions) + warm cache overhead. If you have TTL/eviction patterns share them.
  3) GPU SKUs: for mixed short/medium token workloads H100 96GB (or equivalent) is a good latency-first option; A100-80GB or 80GB Ampere variants with bfloat/quantization profiles are cost-effective for high-throughput read-heavy workloads. We'll include both latency-optimized and cost-optimized SKU scenarios in the initial pass.

Propose a 30-min call Wednesday (Aug 12) 10am PT to review the template and the sample. If that works I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Dylan.Brooks@redwood.com

Thanks Carl / Samantha — great data. A few quick notes from pre-sales sizing:

- Initial sizing assumptions (ballpark): to meet 450ms p95 for interactive routes with your p95 token lengths, we estimate a latency-first cluster based on H100-class nodes sized for KV residency + 20% headroom for bursts. A cost-first option using A100-80GB with model sharding + aggressive quantization reduces monthly unit cost ~28% but increases tail latency by ~30-50ms in our sims.
- Concurrency modeling: because you have a high single-request RPS profile during bursts, we recommend per-route concurrency caps (interactive endpoints) and a separate long-form pool. That reduces queueing and keeps p95 tight.
- Commit sizing ask: to guarantee the 2x ramp and the observed peak, we recommend a 12-month reserved fleet equivalent to 48 H100-class vGPUs (or 64 A100-80GB equivalent) with an initial canary of 8 nodes. We'll formalize exact vCPU/memory and NIC needs after you return the completed template.

Open questions for procurement/security:
- Are there specific KMS/HSM integration requirements for your Private deployment path? (we'll need key rotation SLAs)
- Do you require audit log retention beyond our standard 13 months?

HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example/deal/ORN-2026-07 — I'm linking the sizing draft there and the drive folder with the modeling outputs.

I'll attach a short PDF with the two SKU scenarios (proposed-fleet-sku-options.pdf). If you confirm the commit horizon and KMS needs, we can generate a draft commercial and an initial SLA addendum.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
